t: Number of Substrings With Fixed Ratio — Prefix Balance
o: A substring (l..r] has zero-count z and one-count o with z:o = num1:num2, i.e., num2·z − num1·o = 0 (coprimality guarantees exactness). Define a running score D = num2·(#zeros) − num1·(#ones). A substring has the right ratio exactly when D is equal at its two ends. So sweep s, count how many earlier positions had the same D value using a hash map. Example 1 (num1:num2 = 1:2): four pairs of equal-D prefixes exist → 4.
k: Transform ratio condition into equality of a linear prefix statistic.
Hash map from statistic value to occurrence count; at each position add the count of matching earlier prefixes.

a.i: Sweep left to right maintaining D = num2·zeros − num1·ones. Before processing each character, add cnt[D] to the answer (each earlier prefix with the same D forms a valid substring ending here), then update D and cnt. Seed cnt[0]=1 for the empty prefix. Every substring is counted exactly once at its right end.
s: For each character: first ans += cnt.get(D,0).
Update D += num2 if '0' else -=num1; cnt[D] += 1.
a.t: O(n) — one pass with O(1) expected hash operations.
a.sp: O(n) — hash map of distinct statistic values.

w: Order matters: query the map BEFORE updating D with the current character, and seed the empty-prefix entry. Coprimality ensures the linear equation captures the ratio exactly (no scaled-down ambiguity issues). Return type is 64-bit since answers reach ~n²/2 ≈ 5e9. Follow-up: count substrings with ratio at least/at most num1:num2 — the same statistic with a BIT over compressed values works.
